items.title: No more AI & Taking my Tech Back (A new start for the channel)
items.description: AI is everywhere now, over the last 8 months, I realised it was ruining my hobbies and my critical thinking. From generating Unreal Engine 5 games & letting Claude run my entire home server infrastructure to the point where I couldn't even troubleshoot a simple ZimaBoard ethernet port mix-up, I have become a full-time prompt engineer instead of a tech enthusiast and that gave me zero feeling of accomplishment. More importantly, as a dad, I realised I don't want to raise my son in a world where his dad needs a chatbot to solve every problem. I want to teach him critical thinking, and I can't do that if AI has damaged mine. So, I am taking my tech back. All my AI tools are going into "learning mode" to act as assistants, not the captain with all they keys. Going forward, this channel is changing. We are focusing on human-made setups, physical media, raw hardware reviews, and getting the most out of your money. If you want to use AI to follow along, I'll still provide a prompt in the description, but the videos will focus on doing things by hand. It’s time to add human effort back into tech. I hope you stick around for this new era. Check out Real Good AI: https://www.realgoodai.org/

items.title: I Turned My Old Phone Into an AI Server
items.description: I found my old Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra in a drawer and turned it into an always on local AI server. Ollama, n8n and Termux, all running on the phone itself. No PC, no cloud subscription, and I can text it over normal SMS from anywhere in the world. ⏱️ CHAPTERS 0:00 - The phone in the drawer 0:23 - Proving what this actually is 0:38 - The three free apps you need 1:37 - Picking a model that fits 1:59 - How fast is a phone GPU 2:32 - Texting it from another phone 3:23 - I turn the home network off 4:34 - Inside the automation 7:03 - The local brain and the backup brain 7:44 - What else it can control 8:54 - Where this goes next An unrooted Exynos S22 Ultra, a 1.9GB AI model, and free apps from F-Droid. Round trips came back between 1.758 and 6.31 seconds. 🖥️ WHAT'S RUNNING ON IT Termux • Termux:API • Termux:Boot • Ollama with Vulkan GPU acceleration • Qwen2.5 3B • n8n • DeepInfra as a fallback brain 📺 WATCH NEXT Why I Stopped Using OpenClaw and Built My Own Got an old phone sat in a drawer? Tell me which one and I'll tell you if it would run this. #homeserver #localai #ollama #termux #selfhosted

items.title: My Home Server Runs at 47.7°C. Here's What I'd Change
items.description: Four months ago I made the ZimaBoard2 my home server and I've run it 24/7 ever since. This is what four months of daily use actually looks like: the temperatures, the one bug that still catches me out, and what I've decided to do about the OS. Not sponsored. IceWhale haven't been in touch, so this is entirely my own take on the hardware, ZimaOS, and whether I'd still buy one. ⏱️ CHAPTERS 0:00 - Four months with the ZimaBoard2 0:34 - Let's talk about the temperature 2:22 - The bits I'd keep 3:35 - ZimaOS and the web UI 4:21 - Where it fought me 5:37 - My NAS setup: files, photos and backups 7:12 - Editing YouTube videos straight off the server 7:58 - Claude Code over SSH, a genuine superpower 8:58 - Living with ZimaOS 10:38 - Do I recommend it? 12:03 - What I'm doing next Four months of daily use, one real gripe, and a decision about the OS at the end. 🖥️ WHAT'S RUNNING ON MINE 18TB across two drives • ZimaSpace file sync • Jellyfin • MakeMKV • MegaRipper • Perforce server • Photo backup from mobile • Claude Code over SSH • Docker containers via the ZimaOS app store 🌡️ THE READINGS Chassis 47.7°C • Sides 46.8°C • Rear 45.2°C • Drives 51.6°C • Fan 36°C 📺 WATCH NEXT I Turned My Windows PC Into a Console - No Linux Required https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VYOGL6Sx2pM Got a ZimaBoard? Tell me what yours runs at and whether the USB drives behave themselves for you. #zimaboard #homeserver #selfhosted #nas #zimaos

items.title: The £35 CeX Home Server
items.description: Can a £35 home server actually work? I bought the cheapest PC in CeX, a B-grade Dell OptiPlex 7010 with an i3, 8GB of DDR3 and a 320GB hard drive that sounds like it's begging for retirement, and tried to turn it into a budget home server running Jellyfin, Audiobookshelf and Navidrome. Everyone says old office PCs make great cheap home servers. So I put it to the test. Can it actually self-host a media server, or is it destined for the e-waste pile? ⏱️ CHAPTERS 0:00 - I bought CeX's cheapest PC 1:25 - Unboxing the £35 OptiPlex 7010 2:27 - What's inside this thing? 3:44 - Does it even boot? 7:18 - Benchmarking a potato (3DMark) 9:02 - Building the media server (Jellyfin, Audiobookshelf & Navidrome) 12:11 - The verdict 12:39 - So what do I do with it? 🖥️ WHAT I INSTALLED Jellyfin, free media server Audiobookshelf, podcasts & audiobooks Navidrome, self-hosted music streaming 💰 THE SPECS (£35, B-grade) Dell OptiPlex 7010 SFF i3-3240 @ 3.4GHz 8GB DDR3 320GB HDD Windows 10 No Wi-Fi, no HDMI, no shame Would an SSD have saved it? Probably. Did I have one? No. Let me know in the comments what I should buy from CeX next. #homeserver #cex #budgetpc #selfhosted #jellyfin

items.title: I Put Michael Scott and Minecraft Steve in an AI Group Chat
items.description: In this video, I install SillyTavern and use DeepSeek via DeepInfra's API to build custom AI characters, including Michael Scott from The Office and Minecraft Steve, then put them all in one group chat to see what happens. AI content is dominated by coding agents and productivity tools, so I wanted to try the weirder side: character AI you run yourself, with full control over personality, lore, and memory. Total cost for the entire video: less than one cent. 🛠️ What's in this video: 00:00 - Two AIs Meet Each Other 00:11 - What Is SillyTavern? 01:22 - Installing It 02:52 - Hooking Up DeepSeek (The Cheap Way) 03:18 - Talking to an AI Cat 04:47 - Creating Michael Scott 06:37 - How Much Has This Cost So Far? 07:21 - Teaching Him the Entire Office 08:28 - Minecraft Steve Arrives 09:13 - Putting Them All in One Group Chat 10:23 - The Final Cost 💲 💬 Let me know in the comments: what character would you build first, and should I try this fully locally next time? items.description: 💻 Testing out the new Siri AI macOS 27 developer beta! If you ask the new Siri to write code, it immediately hits a system restriction and shuts you down. items.title: Stop using Claude Code: OpenCode is free!
items.description: In this video, I install the OpenCode desktop app and use a completely free 355-billion parameter model called "Big Pickle" (GLM 4.5) to build a fully functional, playable 80s arcade simulator from scratch. AI tools are getting incredibly expensive, with Anthropic pushing Claude Code to a $100 tier (since reverted) and GitHub Copilot removing models for students. I canceled my pro plan and decided to test OpenCode, a free alternative that acts like a hybrid of Claude Code and Gemini CLI. No paid API calls, no monthly subscriptions, just genuinely powerful AI coding. (200 requests per 5-hour window) 🛠️ What's in this video: 00:00 - The AI Pricing Problem & Copilot Limits 01:22 - Installing the OpenCode Desktop App 02:44 - Planning an Arcade Game with "Big Pickle" 05:41 - Live Debugging & Auto-Fixing Crashes 08:49 - The Final Gameplay Test & Conclusion --- 💬 Let me know in the comments: Are you sticking with paid subscriptions for tools like Copilot and Claude, or are you moving to free/self-hosted alternatives? --- My Setup: - Machine: Mac Mini M4 (Base Model) - Platform: OpenCode Desktop App - Model: GLM 4.5 ("Big Pickle") 🔗 Links & Tools: - OpenCode GitHub: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode - OpenCode: https://opencode.ai/ #OpenCode #ClaudeCode #GitHubCopilot #AI #Coding #Python #GLM4 #DeveloperTools

items.title: Don't Throw Away Your Old 3D Printer. Do THIS Instead.
items.description: Using my dedicated home server, Docker Compose, and the OctoPrint container, I tried turning this "dumb" SD-card reliant 3D printer into a fully remote-controlled 3D printing powerhouse. In this video, I walk through what the software actually is, how to configure the Docker container, mapping the USB devices, showing off live PS5 camera feed, testing the remote hardware controls, and the hilarious reality of what happens when you accidentally scale a test print down by 75%. And yes, it’s incredibly powerful, and the best part is it breathes entirely new life into outdated hardware. 🔗 Links & Tools: • OctoPrint: https://octoprint.org/ • Docker Compose Setup: https://github.com/OctoPrint/octoprint-docker 💬 Let me know in the comments Would you rather self-host an OctoPrint server for an old printer, or just save up for a new BambuLab? 🖥️ My setup in this video: • Artillery Genius (Standard) • N95 Mini PC • PlayStation 5 HD Camera (with custom Linux drivers) • OctoPrint (Official Docker Image) #3DPrinting #OctoPrint #SelfHosted #HomeLab #Docker #ArtilleryGenius #TechDIY #Maker

items.title: Perplexity Computer: $50 for 40 Minutes of Work. Is It Worth It?
items.description: I got my hands on the new Perplexity Computer, so naturally, I did the sensible thing and tried to see how fast it could burn through my wallet while building a game from scratch. Using Perplexity Computer, its new orchestrator model, and up to 19 parallel AI agents, I tried turning a single prompt into a fully functional "Home Server Simulator" game built with HTML, CSS, and JS. In this video, I walk through what the tool actually is, how to get access, watching the AI agents code in parallel, testing the generated game, and the shocking reality of what happens when you let an AI run wild with your credit balance. items.title: ZimaBoard2 Review: I Replaced My Home Server with It… and Added a GPU
items.description: I finally got my hands on the ZimaBoard 2, so naturally I did the sensible thing and tried replacing my entire home server with it. items.title: I Turned My Windows PC Into a Console - No Linux Required
items.description: My PS5 died and I got tired of waiting for Valve to release SteamOS on PC. So I built my own console, on Windows. Command: reg ADD "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\PasswordLess\Device" /v DevicePasswordLessBuildVersion /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f Using Microsoft's hidden Full Screen Experience from the latest Windows Dev builds (Project Helix), I turned a regular PC into a full console setup. No desktop, no explorer.exe, just straight into Steam Big Picture with a DualSense controller. Boot to game in under 30 seconds with up to 800MB less RAM usage than a normal Windows desktop. And unlike Linux or SteamOS, every game works. Fortnite, Valorant, CS2, anything with kernel-level anti-cheat. No Proton, no compatibility layers, no praying. In this video I walk through the full setup from a fresh Windows install to a working console experience using Xbox Full Screen Experience, AnyFSE, and Steam Big Picture. No Microsoft account required on the machine itself. 🔗 Links & Tools: • AnyFSE: https://github.com/ashpynov/AnyFSE • Xbox Full Screen Experience Tool: https://github.com/8bit2qubit/XboxFullScreenExperienceTool • Windows Insider Program: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/windowsinsider/ ⏱️ Timestamps: 0:00 - The finished console in action 0:14 - Why Windows and not Linux 0:35 - What is Full Screen Experience (Project Helix) 1:52 - Windows install & Microsoft account bypass 3:32 - Passwordless auto-login setup 4:25 - Windows Insider Dev Channel enrollment 5:21 - Xbox Insider Hub & PC Gaming Preview 5:39 - Installing AnyFSE & Xbox FSE Tool 8:10 - Configuring Full Screen Experience 8:27 - Choosing Steam Big Picture as home app 9:03 - Custom boot splash screen setup 10:00 - First boot into the console 11:05 - Task Manager proof — RAM savings 11:42 - Benchmark: FSE vs Desktop mode 12:36 - Final thoughts 💬 If you find a fix for the Xbox gamepad keyboard popping up alongside Steam's keyboard sometimes, drop it in the comments, I tried everything. 🎮 My build: • CPU: Ryzen 5 5600X • GPU: RTX 3080 10gb • RAM: 32GB DDR4 3600mhz • Controller: DualSense (PS5) • Capture Card: Elgato 4K X #WindowsConsole #PCGaming #FullScreenExperience #SteamBigPicture #ProjectHelix #NoLinux #ConsolePC #AnyFSE #DualSense #Windows11

items.title: I Gave My Local AI New Tools With MCP Clients (Gerald 2.0 Ep.4)
items.description: Gerald gets a serious upgrade today. We're replacing the single SSH tool with MCP servers, giving Gerald direct access to your file system, web search, GitHub, Ollama models, and Postgres. All self-hosted, all running in Docker alongside n8n. ✅ In this episode: - What MCP is and why it matters for local AI agents - Setting up 5 MCP servers in Docker Compose with Supergateway - Brave Search API setup (free tier, no spend required) - GitHub token setup for repo access - Wiring everything into Gerald Tools in n8n - Live demo - Gerald listing Ollama models via MCP 📁 GitHub: https://github.com/NathsServer/Gerald-Series/tree/main/Episode%204 🚀 CHAPTERS: 0:00 - Intro & What Gerald Tools Can Now Do 0:56 - Updating Docker Compose With MCP Services 3:22 - Getting Your Brave & GitHub API Keys 4:34 - Adding MCP Client Tool Nodes in n8n 11:06 - Live Demo & What's Coming Next 📺 Ep.3 - Gerald Gets a Web UI & PWA App: https://youtu.be/bKc5RvnR0L8 💬 Need help? @NathsServer on Instagram #SelfHosting #HomeLab #LocalAI #n8n #Ollama #MCP #AIAgent #Gerald #Docker
